name: Kinetic
reference: DIA Studio's kinetic typography: words fill the frame, scaled, cropped and stacked to the beat.
pattern: Black, white and one cobalt blue used on a single word.
personality: Type is the motion. Words fill the frame and cut on the beat.

motion.character: Fast and percussive: 4-8 frames per word, scale pops, masked rolls, wraps around the frame.
motion.transitions: Cut on the beat; a word grows to fill the frame and becomes the next ground.

grammar: Words fill the frame edge to edge; cropping is allowed.
Every cut lands on a beat.
The accent colours one word per phrase.

pictures.note: A picture flashes for one beat between words, full frame; the type is the motion.

footage.note: A one-beat flash of footage at most.

music.feel: driving electronic, four on the floor, punchy

hits.note: No effects: the cuts land on the music's beats, and the music carries them.

compose.how: The words are the subject: kineticWords fills the text-safe box; no other subject shares the frame.

hook.how: The first word fills the frame edge to edge on frame 0, cropped by the frame, on the beat.

moves.move: Display type bleeds edge to edge, cropped by the frame on purpose.

measurable.how: Ink covers at least 60 % of the frame width on most beats.

moves.move: The accent word grows until it fills the frame and becomes the next ground.

measurable.how: The accent covers more than 90 % of a frame at a scene change.

moves.move: Every cut lands on a beat.

measurable.how: Cuts sit within 1 frame of a beat.

moves.move: Motion blur along the direction of travel on the fastest moves.

props.phrases: one per beat, accent on one word; the reveal phrase `reveal: true` (the hero size: the largest type of the film); `exit: "toGround"` on the accent phrase before a ground change

blocks.for: Words that fill the frame and bleed; the accent word that grows until it fills the frame and becomes the next ground.

props.then: the stack's next place on each beat

blocks.for: A word that stays and moves while the next one enters.
A ground change on the beat, behind the words (a colour that stays is a ground; a wipe crosses the frame and leaves).
A number that counts in on the beat at display size.

props.color: "accent" for a ground change; "ground" for the end

blocks.for: A ground change on the beat; and the end: a hard cut to the ground on the bar after the last line.

props.whips: a 5-frame whip on the transition, blurred along its travel

blocks.for: The whip between scenes, with motion blur.
Words that replace each other at one cap height, baseline and left edge.

avoid.why: Kinetic speaks in words, not charts.

ends.how: The last line lands on the track's loudest bar, then a hard cut to the ground on the bar. No static restatement. The drop on the reveal wins over this: when no loudest bar falls after the reveal in the film's window, the last line lands on the next strong bar after the reveal (a bar of `beats().bars`, or a cut point of `beats().cuts`), and the cut to the ground comes on the bar after it.
ends.with: `color: "ground"`, `enter: "cut"`, `at` on the bar after the last line: the hard cut to the ground, no hold

mix.note: Driving, four on the floor. No effects: the cuts land on the kick, and the music carries them.

shots.match: Flash pictures share one grade, through the inks.

subjectsToAvoid: Fibonacci numbers or the golden spiral
FizzBuzz or a sort of ten numbers
